transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-11 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Evan (CS), Liam (BrightWave), Priya (BrightWave), Sofia (BrightWave security), Noah, Anita

Summary: quick weekly sync to review recent perf runs on staging, confirm remaining access and security prerequisites, and align on tuning plan for the next canary. We hit better tail latency after changing the batching window but saw increased token spend on long context traces. Action items and next steps captured below.

Topics: onboarding progress; SSO/KMS status; KV cache warming & prefix cache; latency vs cost tradeoffs; quantized model canary; monitoring/alerts; rollout plan

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: All right hi everyone thanks for joining. I think we have, uh, a full house — great. Quick round on who we have — Jordan from Redwood, Maya our SE, Evan on CS, and then BrightWave squad — Liam, Priya, Sofia, Anita and Noah.
[00:18] Liam: Yep hi hi, thanks. We're excited to see the numbers. We ran the new staging workload overnight so we have a couple of questions.
[00:27] Maya: Great, thanks. Quick note: I posted the benchmark spreadsheet in the shared drive, link in the calendar notes, but Jordan I'll resend after the call.
[00:36] Priya: I wasn't sure which sheet was the raw logs vs the summarized numbers, there were a few tabs.
[00:41] Jordan: The CSV called "staging-raw-0307.csv" is the raw qps/latency dumps; the summary tab is "0307-aggregates". Sorry sometimes the export names are messy.
[00:52] Sophia: (laughs) yep we've seen that.
[00:55] Noah: Quick thing on infra — Anita pushed a change to the firewall yesterday to allow egress to Redwood control plane but we haven't tested token exchange yet.
[01:05] Anita: Correct, the peering is up, but the app team needs service account keys from Redwood to run the canary.
[01:12] Jordan: We can provision a short-lived service account and rotate keys; that's the normal flow for Dedicated-like pilots. We'll also support the VPC passthrough once SSO is verified.
[01:23] Priya: On SSO — our IdP team said they saw a SAML metadata ping but we haven't imported it because of a mismatch on the certificate thumbprint.
[01:31] Maya: Ah, that's usually the cert roll problem. We'll re-export metadata with the latest cert — Jordan can you confirm which thumbprint to expect?
[01:38] Jordan: Sure I'll paste the expected thumbprint in the follow-up email, it's SHA256: a3:... (garbled) — I'll send it.
[01:45] [02:02] Liam: On the benchmark summary we noticed 95th percentile latency went from 180ms to ~240ms when we enabled the longer context traces — is that expected?
[02:11] Maya: There's a couple moving parts — enabling context prefetch increased KV cache hits so token generation was faster on average, but longer traces increase attention compute nonlinearly. We tuned the batching window from 20ms to 60ms which helped throughput but created a few tail spikes under burst.
[02:31] Priya: Is that the batching window on the client or on the runtime?
[02:35] Maya: Runtime-level adaptive batching; it's configurable by policy per route. We also saw that the prefix cache wasn't warming because your traffic pattern has a high number of unique conversation IDs, so KV cache hit rate is only about 42%.
[02:49] Liam: Right because we seed a new conversation for each patient session so the prefixes vary.
[02:55] Maya: Exactly, so two levers: adjust application to reuse conversation contexts where safe, or we can change cache eviction/TTL and pre-populate for the first N users to bump hit-rate. Pre-warming does cost tokens though.
[03:07] Sofia: From security side we need KMS integration — we can't allow keys to be managed by Redwood. We require CMKs in our AWS account and an IAM policy that restricts usage to the Redwood service principal.
[03:18] Jordan: We support customer-managed keys (CMK) — we only need the key ARN and a grant that allows Encrypt/Decrypt for the Redwood service principal.
[03:26] Priya: Also need to confirm audit log retention — how long does Redwood keep the full access logs for Private pilots?
[03:33] Evan: For Private we can provision a longer retention (90/365 days depending on tier). For Hosted pilot it's 30 days by default but we can push exports. I'll capture your preferred window — Sofia?
[03:41] Sofia: We prefer 180 days for the pilot until we complete SOC2 questionnaire.
[03:46] Evan: Noted — we'll flag that with Security.
[03:49] [04:12] Noah: About the quantized variant — you suggested a 4-bit quant for the smaller model to save cost. We saw quality drift on one of our classification prompts.
[04:21] Maya: Yes, quantization can change probability mass on edge tokens; our recommendation is to A/B sample with 5k prompt set first, compare ROC/AUC and hallucination rate. In the last run we saw a 0.8% delta in top-1 accuracy on the classification set.
[04:36] Liam: 0.8% might be acceptable but we need to define an SLO for that.
[04:40] Jordan: Agree — define quality SLO first. If it's below 1% delta, we can do a gradual canary with 10% traffic for 48 hours then 50% then full. If it's >1.5% we probably need to try a different quant profile or larger model.
[04:55] Priya: Can you share the exact evaluation harness so we can run locally?
[04:58] Maya: Yes — I added the eval harness link in the sheet; it's a lightweight script and a Docker image. I'll also export the raw seeds.
[05:05] [07:00] Liam: The cost numbers — token cost jumped because the runtime emitted some repeated prompts for context stitching. Any idea why?
[07:10] Maya: We saw duplicate prefix material in the client calls — looks like the SDK is re-sending the system prompt on every partial call. That increases token usage for multi-turn flows. Priya, can your devs look at the SDK usage? We can help with a small patch.
[07:22] Priya: Yes that's on our backlog, I can get a PR opened today.
[07:26] Anita: For the canary we prefer a short maintenance window at night; can Redwood throttle fallback to a smaller model if the quantized variant spikes?
[07:36] Jordan: Yes we support automatic fallback policies; we can route to the float 16 model for higher latency but lower failure rates. We'll add a canary policy that falls back on 95th percentile over threshold.
[07:46] [10:00] Maya: One more infra note — we attempted a KV cache warm test but the prefix key encoding had a character truncation issue which made keys mismatch between client and runtime. That was a minor bug in the SDK that we've already patched in the staging branch.
[10:15] Priya: Good to know. Is there a rolling restart required to pick that up?
[10:20] Maya: No, it's a client-side fix; just update the SDK and the prefix keys align immediately, which should improve hit rate.
[10:27] [15:00] Jordan: Let's walk through the checklist — SSO (in progress, need cert thumbprint), KMS (customer CMK required), VPC peering firewalls (done but token exchange untested), service account (Redwood to create short-lived credentials), dashboard access (Maya to grant), canary timing (tentative Mon), monitoring alerts (thresholds to define).
[15:28] Priya: On the dashboard — can you show 95th tail latency split by seq len? That would be super useful.
[15:33] Maya: Yes we have an existing panel, I'll add a split by token-length bucket and a KV hit overlay.
[15:40] Liam: Also add a token-cost per request metric so we can correlate cost to latency.
[15:45] Maya: Good idea.
[15:48] [20:00] Sofia: A quick compliance point — we need to include the ability to rotate KMS grants monthly and have proof of rotation for SOC2. Does Redwood surface rotation logs?
[20:10] Evan: We can surface KMS grant events in the audit logs and provide an export. We don't perform rotation in your account — you'll rotate, and Redwood will keep the audit entries.
[20:18] Sofia: Ok please note audit export format as JSON lines.
[20:21] Jordan: We'll include a sample export in the follow-up.
[20:24] [24:00] Liam: Any surprises in the staging perf runs? We noticed a 2% error increase during a traffic spike at 03:00 UTC.
[24:10] Maya: That was the batching window ramp combined with a suboptimal kernel selection for token lengths >1024. The runtime selected a fallback kernel which is slower; our team already pushed a kernel hint to prefer the long-seq optimized kernel for that model in staging.
[24:28] Liam: Great. Was there any memory pressure observed?
[24:32] Maya: Memory was stable, but the GC on the runtime host peaked briefly — we've added a guardrail to prevent concurrent heavy encodings during the canary.
[24:40] [30:00] Priya: About observability — can we get logs tagged with customer_account and route id? We need that for our internal correlation tooling.
[30:08] Evan: Yes — we can include account, project, route_id, model_version in each log line. We'll export as structured JSON.
[30:16] Noah: Will those logs include the text payload? We need to ensure PHI doesn't leak into logs.
[30:22] Sofia: Right — PHI is a non-starter for logs.
[30:26] Jordan: By default we redact request bodies from logs for the pilot; you can opt-in to full logs for debugging with a signed DPA addendum. For PHI we'll keep redaction enforced.
[30:40] [38:00] Liam: Ok last big question — timeline. We're aiming to start the canary next week and then go to production in 6 weeks if all goes well. Is that plausible?
[38:12] Jordan: Timeline looks tight but doable: finish SSO + KMS next week, push SDK fix and confirm KV hit-rate improvement, run canary for 48 hours and review evals, then plan phased rollout. So six weeks is achievable if Priya's team and Anita can turn around the infra tasks quickly.
[38:30] Priya: We can prioritize SAML import and KMS details this week.
[38:36] Anita: I'll confirm firewall rules and open the egress ports by Friday.
[38:40] Maya: We'll schedule the canary and notify you of the exact maintenance window — aiming for Mon 2027-03-15 03:00-05:00 UTC but we'll confirm once SSO/KMS are green.
[38:52] [45:00] Jordan: Recap of next steps — I'll send the benchmark CSV and a runbook, Maya will add dashboard panels and invite you to read-only, Priya to provide SAML metadata and KMS ARN, Anita to confirm peering details. Evan will follow up on audit retention.
[45:20] Priya: Sounds good. One last ask — can Redwood provide a short security attestation for the pilot (one page) summarizing controls?
[45:29] Evan: Yes we have a pilot security attestation template — I'll attach it to the follow up ticket.
[45:35] Sofia: If possible include the list of data flows and where PHI is handled.
[45:40] Evan: Will do.
[45:44] [51:30] Jordan: Great thanks everyone for the updates, we'll follow up with the spreadsheet and the cert thumbprint. Meeting adjourned.

References mentioned: benchmark spreadsheet (drive link), staging-raw-0307.csv, eval harness Docker image link, pilot security attestation template (link), runbook (link).

End of transcript.
